claim: CodeVetter preserves direct repository callsites for allowlisted promise-based Node async creators while refusing to attribute dependency- or framework-created response-linked work to an application ancestor.

proofs: A direct node:timers/promises call retains server.mjs with node_async_creator_callsite provenance.
A direct node:fs/promises read retains server.mjs with the same provenance while preserving the operation result.
A dependency-owned timer remains source-null even though the application handler is an ancestor.
No private timer value, filesystem path, dependency label, or raw async identity enters evidence.

diagnosis.result: The framework-created timer stayed unattributed; CodeVetter did not promote the static page owner or another application ancestor as its creator.

limitations: The real product run used a local config-disabled Next development runtime and does not establish production performance.
The public async inventory was sampled to eight resources and cannot support absence claims.
